text:
maria: heads-up — customers in eu-west-1 are seeing 502s to the analytics ingestion service behind our PrivateLink. Traces show connection resets after TLS handshake. Anyone familiar with vpce oddness?
aj: can you post the vpce id and whether Private DNS is enabled?
maria: vpce-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h, Private DNS: true. It resolves to 10.0.45.12 (one of the interface ENIs).
sam: quick checklist: 1) endpoint SG allows inbound from callers? 2) endpoint ENI in same subnet as callers? 3) route tables not relevant for interface endpoints but check NACLs.
maria: SG on the endpoint only allows inbound from sg-cluster-nodes (sg-0abc). Our EKS pods have pod IPs in 10.232.0.0/16 which are not members of that SG. We assumed node SG was enough.
nora: ah — with the Amazon VPC CNI, pod IPs are Src IPs for ENI traffic. If endpoint SG allows only node SG, traffic from pods will be dropped unless nodes SNAT. Do we SNAT pods?
aj: we turned off SNAT on nodes to preserve client IP for logging. So pod IPs are used. Endpoint SG needs to allow pod CIDR or the cluster node SG should be applied to the endpoint ENI.
maria: I tried adding 10.232.0.0/16 -> endpoint SG inbound tcp 443 and it made errors go away for a bit, then it started flapping again with TLS errors.
sam: could be cross-account NLB target behavior — if the backend NLB is in another account, it might be checking client cert or expecting source IP to be from our node SG. Also ensure the endpoint is configured for the correct service name (svc name across account) and the NLB has health checks from the endpoint IPs.
ora: run tcpdump on the endpoint ENI and capture the failed TLS handshake packets. Also check aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces for that ENI to see which subnet and AZ it's in.
maria: ran tcpdump, seeing SYN, SYN-ACK, then client sends ClientHello and server responds RST. Backend NLB logs show 200ms latency before reset.
aj: that pattern suggests the backend is rejecting connections after SNI check or ALPN mismatch. Can you reproduce with curl --resolve to the private IP and verbose TLS?
maria: curl --resolve analytics.example.internal:443:10.0.45.12 -v shows TLS server cert for the NLB target (different CN). It seems Private DNS returns the endpoint IP, but the SNI still has public name and backend rejects.
sam: two options: 1) update endpoint Private DNS mapping or 2) preserve SNI expected by backend by rewriting Host header/SNI at the endpoint (not supported). Best fix is to ensure the backend accepts the same SNI or we use a dedicated internal certificate. Also confirm the endpoint's private DNS isn't returning NLB IPs in some fallback.
maria: Meanwhile, rolling a short-term workaround: re-enable SNAT on nodes so source IP is node IP and revert SG to node SG only. That reduced errors in the last 10m.
ora: long-term, let's: - update endpoint SG to include pod CIDR (security review required) OR - request the backend team to accept SNI from our internal hostnames OR - move service behind regional ALB in same account.
ora: tagging @sam for design decision, @aj for security sign-off.
ing-ops-bot: automation: vpn-checker run — no cross-VPC route leaks detected.
maria: action items: I will keep SNAT enabled for now and open a ticket to coordinate with backend on cert/SNI. I'll post the tcpdump capture in the ticket. Thanks all :thumbsup:
